static_traits.name: Wen Jie
static_traits.family_status: Parents live across the street, usually in touch, but this specific issue not yet discussed with them
static_traits.social_status: Relationship with a friend becomes strained and alienated due to his frequent criticism of book endings
static_traits.medical_history: without previous similar psychological problems;not yet received psychotherapy;without significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe reading experiences and details specifically;tends to focus on negative details and use absolute evaluations (like 'wasting time''ruining everything');attitude somewhat negative but cooperation acceptable

basic_info.main_problem: I often feel disappointed and frustrated after finishing a book, especially when the ending does not meet my expectations.This dissatisfaction started months ago and has worsened;I keep criticizing the endings and have lost the joy of reading.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent disappointment and frustration have affected overall mood and leisure experience, hoping through counseling to reduce negative filtering, restore enjoyment of reading, and improve emotions.

core_beliefs: If the ending does not meet my expectations, the whole book is utterly without value
Leisure activities must be a complete and 'perfect' experience, otherwise it is a waste of time

special_situations.event: After finishing a book, finding the ending rushed or not yet echoing the earlier setup
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the ending does not meet my raised expectations, all previous investment is wasted
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: When evaluating, focusing on the negative ending and negating the earlier strengths to avoid being disappointed again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This book made me read in vain; I wasted my time.

special_situations.event: When discussing books with friends, friends say 'find better books' and struggle to understand their dissatisfaction
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others do not agree with my evaluation or do not understand my disappointment, I will be seen as a complainer
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Insists on a critical ending to prove one's point, reducing in-depth communication with friends
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They do not understand me; they are probably already tired of me.

special_situations.event: Academic pressure increases; expectations of reading as relaxation grow higher
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Under high pressure, leisure activities must fully meet expectations, otherwise they cannot relieve stress
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Setting higher standards for books; once the ending is not good, negating the whole book
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No book can satisfy me now.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to gain reliable relaxation and satisfaction through reading, and to keep positive experiences fully preserved
core_conflict.fear: Fearing betrayed investment, wasted time, disappointment, emotional loss of control
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of control through harsh criticism and negation, avoiding being hurt by disappointment again

object_relations.self_representation: A misunderstood harsh critic / disappointed reader
object_relations.object_representation: Others who do not understand and give perfunctory advice (friends)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others (such as the counselor or a friend) invite them to recall the positive parts of the book, or offer a balancing view on their judgment that 'the whole book was a waste'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to think the other person is negating his feelings and ignoring his disappointment (projecting one's own experience of being let down onto others' 'not understanding' intentions)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a calm, organized tone, lists the logical flaws and holes in the ending, downplays or skips subjective feelings; avoids touching the emotional components of positive experiences.

manifestations: Believes the ending 'ruined everything', treats the reading experience as a 'waste of time'
Leisure reading loses its joy, hard to relax
outcomes: Doubting the meaning of leisure activities

manifestations: Not yet having talked about this problem with parents living nearby
outcomes: Increased sense of alienation,Insufficient use of social support

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Attributes feelings of disappointment and being let down to 'the ending ruined everything', finding it hard to recognize her own raised expectations and pressure factors
Believing others 'do not understand' one's dissatisfaction, thereby deepening the alienation

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: When invited to recall positive parts of the book, quickly turns back to the ending's flaws
Difficult to stay with and deepen positive experiences; instead emphasizes the negative

positive_force: Academic performance not yet affected, indicating self-management and task execution abilities are acceptable
Parents live nearby; potential support resources available
Willing to try a balanced perspective and reality testing, with motivation to change
Able to identify and describe the book's strengths (unique plot, character depth)
negative_force: Marked pattern of mental filtering and negating positive thinking
Under high pressure, forms perfectionistic expectations of leisure activities (all-or-nothing standards)
Frequent criticism leads to Interpersonal tension and weakened support
Attributes disappointment mainly to the external (the book's ending), ignoring own expectations and situational factors

target_behavior.behavior: After finishing a book, excessively focusing on and criticizing the ending, negating the whole book, with marked disappointment and frustration
antecedent: Finishing reading and encountering an ending that does not meet anticipation or feels rushed
Recent high Academic pressure, heightened expectations
When discussing books with friends, encountering not being understood or being advised to 'find better books'
target_behavior.core_reason: Under Academic pressure, forming perfectionist and black-and-white evaluation standards, accompanied by mental filtering and negating positive thinking, equating dissatisfaction with the ending to overall failure and wasted time
target_behavior.function: Avoids feelings of disappointment and being let down, maintaining a sense of control over and high expectations of leisure experiences
target_behavior.consequence: Overall Low mood, declining leisure experience and ability to relax;Tense relationships with friends;reduced joy of reading
